questions.q: What is the main job of a baseline forecast in a project?
options: It replaces the final model in production
It gives every later model a bar to clear, so you can tell whether added complexity actually helps
It removes seasonality from the data
It is only needed when there is no training data
questions.explain: A baseline costs almost nothing to build. If a sophisticated model cannot beat it, the extra complexity is not justified.

questions.q: What does a seasonal naive forecast do for daily data with a weekly pattern?
options: Repeats the average of the whole history
Repeats the last observed value for every future day
Repeats the last full 7-day cycle, so each forecast day copies the same weekday from the most recent week
Fits a straight line through the first and last points
questions.explain: Seasonal naive uses a season length (here 7) and copies the most recent season forward. The season length matches the pattern's period.

questions.q: Which baseline follows a steady upward trend by adding the average historical change per step to the last value?
options: Drift
Mean
Naive
Seasonal naive
questions.explain: Drift is naive plus a straight line whose slope is the average change from the first to the last training point.

questions.q: On the lesson's illustrative sales, the mean baseline had an MAE near 99.5 while the others were around 16 to 18. Why was the mean so much worse?
options: The mean baseline used the test data
MAE cannot be computed for the mean
Seasonal patterns make means invalid
Sales trend upward, so the all-time average sits far below recent values
questions.explain: The mean assumes nothing changes over time. With a trending series, the historical average is far from where the series is now.

questions.q: How should you split a series to evaluate a baseline?
options: Hold out the last stretch of the series (for example the final 28 days) and forecast it using only earlier data
Randomly assign each day to train or test
Train on the last 28 days and test on everything earlier
Use the whole series for both training and testing
questions.explain: Forecasts always look forward, so the test window must come after the training data. Random splits leak the future.
